thread:
Maria (support): @Raj FYI - Halcyon reporting a mid-day spike causing ~10-15% 429s and tail latency to jump to 1.8s from 120ms. They say this started at ~11:40 PT during a promo blast. Attached Grafana snapshots: https://grafana.internal/r/halcyon-qps
Raj (eng-oncall): seeing the alert now :rotating_light: can you paste the sample client logs and their pool config?
Maria (support): pasted logs below, customer says baseline QPS ~40, sustained peak ~420 for ~7m, burst >900 for 30s. Their dedicated pool shows 4 nodes, min=2, max=6 in console. They said "we thought reserved burst would kick", but burst capacity was not enabled.
Maria (support): sample errors: 
```
2026-03-17T18:41:12Z ERROR request_id=abc123 code=429 msg="rate_limit_exceeded" route=/v1/generate status=429
2026-03-17T18:41:13Z WARN request_id=abc124 latency_ms=1820 token_out=320
```
Elaine (sre): interesting — autoscaler kept pool at 4 but GPU util hit 92% and IO wait spiked. If min/max are 2/6 we wouldn't scale to 12 even if throughput needs it. Looks like their pool was undersized for their peak profile.
Raj (eng-oncall): confirm: autoscaler policy is "utilization_target=65%" right? If so, when they have many short-lived requests the scaler may miss rapid spikes because our cool_down defaults to 120s. Also prefix caching not helpful for short chat-like requests.
Tim (cs): Halcyon is a mid-size adtech team — they ran an unannounced campaign. We need a quick mitigation + follow-up plan.
Maria (support): quick mitigation options proposed to customer: 1) enable burst capacity (temp +1x) 2) raise max nodes to 12 3) change autoscale policy to faster scaling (cool_down=20s) 4) set per-route rate limit to give graceful 503 fallback instead of 429s. Which is safest now?
Elaine (sre): prioritize enabling burst capacity and raising max nodes. Also drop utilization_target to 55% during campaign window. For medium-term: increase min nodes to 6 so spikes don't always require spin-up.
Raj (eng-oncall): I can push a one-off policy change for them: set max_nodes=12, burst_enabled=true, cool_down=30s. We'll monitor. Can someone request customer approval for potential added cost?
Tim (cs): I messaged Halcyon rep — they approved temporary changes for the next 3 hours. Note: they asked us to add a postmortem and cost estimate.
Maria (support): rolling change now — applying: 
```
pool.apply({
  pool_id: "halcyon-prod-01",
  max_nodes: 12,
  burst_capacity: true,
  autoscale: { utilization_target: 55, cool_down_s: 30 }
})
```
LoadBot: [alert resolved] halcyon-prod-01 autoscale.policy.update by Raj at 1791235123
Raj (eng-oncall): change applied, watching metrics. Initial reaction: QPS handled, 429s dropped to 0 within ~90s, p95 latency back to ~150ms. Still seeing short-lived 400-600 qps microbursts; we'll keep burst_enabled.
Elaine (sre): follow-up items: 1) run a noisy-neighbor check across that rack (gpu-memory fragmentation) 2) add request-size based routing to large-batch path 3) propose a recommended capacity plan for Halcyon: baseline 50 qps, reserved min_nodes=6, max_nodes=12, utilization_target=60, burst_enabled=true.
Maria (support): I'll create the ticket with cost delta estimate and notify billing. Also scheduling a capacity review call with Halcyon tomorrow.
Tim (cs): thanks team. Add the quick repro steps to the ticket for our docs: 
```
# repro (from customer):
for i in {1..1000}; do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -d '{"prompt":"short","max_tokens":64}' & done
```
Elaine (sre): adding note: for capacity planning, use 99th percentile burst QPS and multiply by 0.8 to account for KV/cache hit rates when mapping to node counts.
Maria (support): closing loop with customer: emailed them summary + cost estimate. Will post postmortem after 24h of monitoring. :thumbsup:
summary: Halcyon experienced short-lived high-QPS campaign that exceeded their configured pool max and autoscale cooldown, causing 429s. Team enabled burst capacity, increased max nodes, and lowered utilization target to restore SLA; follow-ups include noisy-neighbor checks and a capacity plan recommendation.
